epithet.en: A foreign professor of black magic visiting Moscow
epithet.da: En udenlandsk professor i sort magi på besøg i Moskva

1.modern-en: A foreign stranger joins Berlioz and Ivan on their bench at Patriarch's Ponds, insists that Jesus existed, and tells Berlioz calmly how his evening will end.

3.modern-en: The professor claims he was present in person on Pilate's balcony, announces that he will stay in Berlioz's apartment, and promises a seventh proof.

4.modern-en: Ivan chases the professor and his two companions across Moscow, but however fast he runs the distance between them never closes.

7.modern-en: Introducing himself as Woland, professor of black magic, he waits for the hungover Styopa with a contract Styopa does not remember signing, and has him removed from apartment No. 50.

9.modern-en: Through his interpreter Koroviev he takes over Berlioz's apartment for the length of his engagement, and the chairman who signs the lease soon regrets it.

12.modern-en: At the Variety he sits in an armchair on stage and watches the Muscovites while his assistants perform, wondering aloud whether the people of Moscow have changed.

13.modern-en: Ivan's neighbor at the clinic hears the story of Patriarch's Ponds and tells Ivan plainly whom he met there.

18.modern-en: In apartment No. 50 he receives the Variety's barman, who has come to complain about worthless takings, and asks him when he expects to die.

22.modern-en: He receives Margarita in his candlelit bedroom, playing chess with Behemoth while Hella rubs ointment into his aching knee, and shows her his globe.

23.modern-en: He appears at the end of the great ball and speaks to the guests who interest him most.

24.modern-en: After the ball he asks Margarita what she wants in return, keeps his word in his own way, and gives the master back his burned novel.

29.modern-en: On a terrace high above Moscow he watches the city at sunset and receives a messenger from Yershalaim with a request about the master.

31.modern-en: On the Sparrow Hills he waits on horseback while the master and Margarita take their leave of Moscow.

32.modern-en: On the night ride his retinue and his guests appear in their true forms, and he shows the master a man who has been waiting for him for a very long time.

33.modern-en: After his departure Moscow tries for years to explain away what happened during his visit.

epithet.en: A lanky, jeering man in a checked jacket, Woland's interpreter
epithet.da: En lang, spottende mand i ternet jakke, Wolands tolk

1.modern-en: A transparent figure in a checked jacket and a jockey cap appears before Berlioz in the heat at Patriarch's Ponds and dissolves again.

3.modern-en: The checked fellow reappears at the Ponds, calls himself a former choirmaster, and points Berlioz toward the turnstile.

4.modern-en: The choirmaster takes the professor's side when Ivan tries to detain him, then leads Ivan on a chase through the city with the professor and the cat.

9.modern-en: As Woland's interpreter he talks Nikanor Ivanovich into letting the apartment, presses money on him, and then makes a telephone call about him.

12.modern-en: Under the name Fagot he runs the show at the Variety, from a rain of banknotes to a shop of Paris fashions for the ladies.

18.modern-en: He receives Berlioz's uncle Poplavsky with loud grief over the dead nephew, and hurries the barman out after Woland has finished with him.

22.modern-en: He meets Margarita and leads her through a staircase and an apartment that are far larger than they should be.

23.modern-en: He stands beside Margarita at the top of the staircase and names each of the guests as they arrive at the ball.

24.modern-en: He helps settle accounts after the ball, and throws the master's case history from the clinic into the fire.

27.modern-en: He and his companions are found having breakfast in apartment No. 50 when the investigators come for them.

28.modern-en: He and Behemoth make a last tour of Moscow, causing a scandal at the Torgsin store and a fire at Griboyedov's.

29.modern-en: He returns with Behemoth to Woland's terrace, reeking of burning, to report on their last escapades.

31.modern-en: He waits on horseback with Woland on the Sparrow Hills.

32.modern-en: On the night ride the clowning choirmaster is gone, and a dark knight rides in his place.

33.modern-en: When the investigation tries to explain the visit, suspicion falls mainly on him as a hypnotist of unprecedented power.

epithet.en: An enormous black cat who talks, drinks and fights in Woland's retinue
epithet.da: En enorm sort kat i Wolands følge, der taler, drikker og slås

4.modern-en: A cat as big as a hog tries to pay its fare on the tram while Ivan is chasing the professor.

7.modern-en: A huge black cat in Styopa's apartment holds a glass of vodka in one paw and a pickled mushroom on a fork in the other.

12.modern-en: At the Variety the cat tears off the master of ceremonies' head on the audience's request.

22.modern-en: He plays chess against Woland, cheats badly and talks his way out of losing.

23.modern-en: He sits at Margarita's feet at the top of the staircase during the ball and keeps interrupting her.

24.modern-en: He shows off his marksmanship after the ball and boasts about his part in the evening.

27.modern-en: He holds off the armed men who storm apartment No. 50 with a Browning and a Primus stove.

28.modern-en: With Koroviev he gorges on mandarins at the Torgsin store and ends the visit by setting Griboyedov House alight.

29.modern-en: He comes back to Woland's terrace with Koroviev, soot-covered and loaded with souvenirs of the fire.

31.modern-en: He waits with Woland on the Sparrow Hills and whistles a farewell over Moscow.

32.modern-en: On the night ride the cat turns out to be someone else altogether.

epithet.en: A short, red-haired, fanged member of Woland's retinue
epithet.da: Et lille, rødhåret medlem af Wolands følge med en hugtand

7.modern-en: A short, red-haired man with a fang steps out of Styopa's mirror and announces that Styopa has no place in the apartment.

10.modern-en: A red-haired man with a fang and a film over one eye helps the cat seize Varenukha outside the theater's lavatory.

18.modern-en: He meets Berlioz's uncle in the apartment and makes clear that he will not be inheriting anything.

19.modern-en: He sits down beside Margarita in the Alexander Garden, knows about her grief, and offers her a way to find out about the master.

20.modern-en: He gives Margarita her instructions by telephone once the cream has worked.

22.modern-en: He is in attendance in Woland's bedroom when Margarita is presented.

24.modern-en: After the ball he questions a man about a complaint written against the master.

27.modern-en: He is in apartment No. 50 with the others when the investigators arrive.

29.modern-en: He stands with Woland on the terrace above Moscow and is given an errand concerning the master and Margarita.

30.modern-en: He visits the master and Margarita in their basement bearing a present from Woland.

31.modern-en: He flies the master and Margarita to the Sparrow Hills in the tail of his cloak.

32.modern-en: On the night ride he too appears in his true form.

epithet.en: Woland's red-haired maid
epithet.da: Wolands rødhårede tjenestepige

10.modern-en: A naked red-haired girl with phosphorescent eyes comes up to Varenukha in apartment No. 50 and kisses him.

14.modern-en: At night a naked girl presses her face to Rimsky's window and reaches through it for the latch.

18.modern-en: Wearing only a lace apron, she opens the door of apartment No. 50 to the Variety's barman.

22.modern-en: She rubs a hot ointment into Woland's knee while he receives Margarita.

23.modern-en: She helps prepare Margarita for the ball.

24.modern-en: She takes part in the supper after the ball, quarrels with the cat and makes up with him.

epithet.en: A former historian who wrote a novel about Pontius Pilate
epithet.da: En tidligere historiker, der har skrevet en roman om Pontius Pilatus

13.modern-en: A nameless patient slips into Ivan's room from the balcony and tells him about his novel about Pilate, the woman he loved, and what the critics did to him.

15.modern-en: In room 118 the clinic's secret patient grows restless at the moon.

19.modern-en: Margarita has not heard from him since autumn and cannot tell whether he is alive or dead.

24.modern-en: He is brought out of the clinic into Woland's presence, worn out and frightened, and finds Margarita there.

27.modern-en: He sleeps peacefully in the basement while Margarita finishes reading his novel.

29.modern-en: Woland and Levi Matvei decide what is to become of him.

30.modern-en: In his old basement he and Margarita try to make sense of what has happened to them, until Azazello pays a call.

31.modern-en: He takes his leave of Moscow from the Sparrow Hills.

32.modern-en: On the night ride Woland shows him the hero of his novel and lets him finish it.

33.modern-en: Ivan, now a historian himself, still dreams of him every spring at the full moon.

epithet.en: The master's beloved, the wife of a prominent Moscow specialist
epithet.da: Mesterens elskede, gift med en fremtrædende specialist i Moskva

13.modern-en: The master tells Ivan about a woman carrying yellow flowers who walked beside him one day and changed his life.

19.modern-en: Unhappy in a comfortable marriage, she wakes from a dream of the master and goes out to the Alexander Garden, where a stranger speaks to her about him.

20.modern-en: She rubs Azazello's cream into her skin and is transformed.

21.modern-en: Invisible and free, she flies over Moscow on a broom, wrecks the apartment of the critic who destroyed the master, and is welcomed by the creatures of the river.

22.modern-en: She is brought to Woland's apartment and agrees to act as hostess of his ball.

23.modern-en: As queen of the ball she stands for hours at the top of the staircase receiving a stream of guests.

24.modern-en: Asked what she wants as her reward, she makes a request that surprises Woland, and then asks for the master.

27.modern-en: She finishes reading the chapter of the master's novel in the basement as morning breaks.

30.modern-en: In the basement she and the master receive a visit from Azazello that changes everything.

31.modern-en: She takes her leave of Moscow from the Sparrow Hills.

32.modern-en: On the night ride she leads the master toward the home that has been promised to them.

33.modern-en: She appears to Ivan every spring in his dreams on the night of the full moon.

epithet.en: A young Moscow poet who writes under the pen name Bezdomny
epithet.da: En ung digter i Moskva, der skriver under pseudonymet Bezdomnyj

1.modern-en: At Patriarch's Ponds he listens to Berlioz explain why his anti-religious poem fails, and is rude to the foreigner who joins them.

3.modern-en: He hears the professor's story, grows suspicious of the stranger, and witnesses what happens to Berlioz at the turnstile.

4.modern-en: He chases the professor and his companions through Moscow, loses his clothes on the bank of the Moscow River, and sets off again with a candle and a paper icon.

5.modern-en: He bursts into the Griboyedov restaurant in his underwear demanding help to catch the consultant, and is tied up.

6.modern-en: At the clinic he tries to explain himself to the doctor and quarrels bitterly with the poet Ryukhin.

8.modern-en: He tells Professor Stravinsky about the consultant and is persuaded to stay at the clinic.

11.modern-en: Trying to write a statement for the police, he finds himself divided between an old Ivan and a new one.

13.modern-en: A stranger enters his room from the balcony, and Ivan promises never to write poetry again.

15.modern-en: He sleeps, and dreams about Bald Mountain.

27.modern-en: He talks to the investigator calmly and indifferently, no longer interested in what happened at Patriarch's Ponds.

30.modern-en: The master and Margarita pay him a last visit at the clinic.

33.modern-en: Years later, as a historian, he walks every spring at the full moon to Patriarch's Ponds.

epithet.en: Chairman of Massolit and editor of a literary magazine
epithet.da: Formand for Massolit og redaktør af et litterært tidsskrift

1.modern-en: On a hot evening at Patriarch's Ponds he lectures Ivan on why Jesus never existed, until a foreigner joins the conversation.

3.modern-en: He sets off to telephone the authorities about the foreigner.

5.modern-en: The writers waiting for him at Griboyedov House wonder why he is late for the meeting.

7.modern-en: He does not answer Styopa's calls in apartment No. 50, and his study door has been sealed.

9.modern-en: His rooms in apartment No. 50 become the object of every tenant's ambitions.

18.modern-en: His uncle arrives from Kiev hoping to inherit his Moscow rooms.

19.modern-en: Margarita watches a funeral procession pass the Alexander Garden.

23.modern-en: He appears at the end of the ball in a form nobody expected.

epithet.en: The Roman procurator of Judea
epithet.da: Judæas romerske prokurator

2.modern-en: Tormented by a headache, the procurator questions a prisoner from Galilee and finds himself drawn into a conversation he does not want to end.

16.modern-en: His sentence is carried out on Bald Mountain under the eyes of his troops.

25.modern-en: As a storm breaks over Yershalaim he receives the head of his secret service and gives him instructions about Judas from Kiriath.

26.modern-en: Alone on the night of the feast he waits for news, receives two visitors and dreams of a moonlit road.

32.modern-en: On the night ride the master finds him sitting on a stone platform in the mountains with his dog, still waiting.

33.modern-en: He goes on appearing in Ivan's dreams at the full moon.

epithet.en: A wandering philosopher brought before Pilate
epithet.da: En omvandrende filosof, der føres frem for Pilatus

2.modern-en: A beaten young prisoner tells Pilate that all people are good, cures his headache, and talks about truth and power with dangerous frankness.

16.modern-en: On Bald Mountain he suffers through the long afternoon in the heat while his only follower watches from the hillside.

26.modern-en: Aphranius reports to Pilate how he behaved at the end and what his last words were.

32.modern-en: Woland tells the master that Yeshua has asked for something on his behalf.

epithet.en: Yeshua's only follower, a former tax collector
epithet.da: Jeshuas eneste discipel, en tidligere tolder

2.modern-en: Yeshua tells Pilate about the tax collector who threw his money into the road to follow him and writes down his words on parchment.

16.modern-en: On the hillside at Bald Mountain he curses himself, then God, as the execution drags on, and makes a desperate plan.

26.modern-en: Brought before Pilate on the night of the feast, he refuses to be bought and makes a threat.

29.modern-en: He appears on Woland's terrace with a message for the devil.

epithet.en: Head of the procurator's secret service
epithet.da: Chef for prokuratorens hemmelige tjeneste

25.modern-en: He comes to Pilate in the storm to report on the execution and leaves with a quiet instruction about Judas from Kiriath.

26.modern-en: He arranges matters in the Lower City on the night of the feast and reports to Pilate afterward.

epithet.en: A young man of Yershalaim who befriended Yeshua
epithet.da: En ung mand i Jersjalaim, der blev ven med Jeshua

2.modern-en: Yeshua tells Pilate about the kind, inquisitive young man who invited him home and asked him what he thought about state power.

25.modern-en: Pilate tells Aphranius he has heard Judas will be killed that night, and asks Aphranius to protect him.

26.modern-en: On the night of the feast he hurries out of the city to meet a woman in the garden at Gethsemane.

epithet.en: Director of the Variety Theater
epithet.da: Direktør for Varietéteatret

7.modern-en: He wakes in apartment No. 50 with a ferocious hangover to find a stranger who says they have signed a contract.

10.modern-en: Telegrams arrive at the Variety claiming that he is in Yalta, only hours after he was seen in Moscow.

14.modern-en: He is still missing while the theater falls into chaos after the show.

27.modern-en: He returns from Yalta and begs the investigators to lock him in an armored cell.

33.modern-en: He is transferred to Rostov to manage a large grocery store and is said to have stopped drinking port.

epithet.en: Financial director of the Variety
epithet.da: Økonomichef ved Varietéen

7.modern-en: Styopa telephones him from apartment No. 50 about money for the foreign magician.

10.modern-en: Rimsky reads impossible telegrams from Yalta about the director and sends Varenukha off with them.

12.modern-en: He watches the black magic show go wrong and rushes to the stricken master of ceremonies.

14.modern-en: Alone in his office after the show, he receives a visit from Varenukha, who is not quite himself.

27.modern-en: He is found in Leningrad hiding in a hotel wardrobe and arrested.

33.modern-en: He resigns from the Variety and joins a children's puppet theater.

epithet.en: Administrator of the Variety
epithet.da: Administrator ved Varietéen

10.modern-en: Sent to the authorities with Styopa's telegrams, he is seized in the theater garden and dragged off to apartment No. 50.

14.modern-en: He comes back to Rimsky's office late at night, pale, casting no shadow and keen to keep the door shut.

17.modern-en: The investigators settle in his empty office at the Variety.

24.modern-en: He comes to Woland after the ball and begs to be let off being a vampire.

27.modern-en: He turns up in Moscow and, despite his promise to Azazello not to lie, begins his statement with a lie.

33.modern-en: He becomes famous for his courtesy on the telephone.

epithet.en: Chairman of the tenants' association at No. 302-bis Sadovaya
epithet.da: Formand for beboerforeningen i Sadovaja nr. 302-bis

9.modern-en: Besieged by tenants after Berlioz's death, he lets the dead man's apartment to a foreigner through Koroviev and takes a fee for his trouble.

15.modern-en: In the clinic he dreams of a theater where an audience is made to hand over its hidden currency.

27.modern-en: Investigators find him in Stravinsky's clinic.

33.modern-en: He comes to hate the theater, the poet Pushkin and the actor Kurolesov.

epithet.en: Margarita's housemaid
epithet.da: Margaritas stuepige

19.modern-en: She asks her mistress what to make for dinner as Margarita sets out for a walk.

20.modern-en: She walks in on Margarita's transformation and wants the cream for herself.

21.modern-en: She catches up with Margarita over the city, riding a hog.

23.modern-en: She is at Margarita's side as Margarita is prepared for the ball.

24.modern-en: After the ball she asks Woland for a favor of her own.

epithet.en: A woman from Sadovaya Street known as the Plague
epithet.da: En kvinde fra Sadovaja kaldet Pesten

1.modern-en: The foreigner says she has already bought sunflower oil and spilled it.

3.modern-en: Hurrying to the turnstile, Berlioz recalls the foreigner's talk about her and the sunflower oil.

4.modern-en: Ivan hears her name in the crowd and links it to the foreigner's prediction.

24.modern-en: Up before dawn in the building on Sadovaya, she has a collision on the stairs and picks something up.

27.modern-en: She is arrested trying to pay for goods with a ten-dollar bill.

epithet.en: Head of the psychiatric clinic
epithet.da: Overlæge på den psykiatriske klinik

8.modern-en: He listens to Ivan's story about the consultant without arguing and persuades him to stay at the clinic.

15.modern-en: Nikanor Ivanovich is brought to his clinic and given an injection on his prescription.

27.modern-en: An investigator comes to his clinic and asks who has been admitted in the last three days.

epithet.en: The high priest, president of the Sanhedrin
epithet.da: Ypperstepræsten, formand for Sanhedrinet

2.modern-en: In the palace garden Pilate asks him which of the condemned the Sanhedrin will release for the feast.

25.modern-en: Pilate and Aphranius discuss the money that Judas is to receive at the high priest's palace that evening.

26.modern-en: His palace is where Judas goes first on the night of the feast.

epithet.en: A giant Roman centurion
epithet.da: En kæmpestor romersk centurion

2.modern-en: Pilate sends for him to teach the prisoner how to address the procurator.

16.modern-en: He commands the century that guards the execution on Bald Mountain.

26.modern-en: He takes his orders from Pilate on the night of the feast.

epithet.en: A journalist who befriended the master
epithet.da: En journalist, der blev mesterens ven

24.modern-en: He is brought before the master and Margarita in his underwear and asked about a complaint he once wrote.

30.modern-en: A visitor calls for him at the basement window, and Margarita says he was arrested yesterday.

33.modern-en: He ends up as the Variety's financial director, in the post Rimsky gave up.
